note: Aspen-Sopris RD, White River NF: small campground in aspen and conifer on the north side of CO-82, ~8 mi east of Aspen at ~9,400 ft, inside the Independence Pass length restriction (no vehicle or combination over 35 ft). Weller Trail and fishing nearby; the Roaring Fork is across the highway. --Claude
summary: FS page (found; stored website was the White River NF home page) + CDOT: confirmed 11 sites, vault toilets, $28, no reservations; added 5-day limit, trash, check-out/occupancy rules, fees checked. Page silent on season and site lengths; it contradicts itself on water (stored false left). Note cleaned and corrected: the campground is inside the CO-82 35-ft restriction, not below it.

Phone: none stored. Aspen-Sopris Ranger District, 620 Main Street, Carbondale, (970) 963-2266 (White River NF offices page; the campground page lists only the Supervisor's Office 970-945-2521).

CO-82 length limit: the FS page says 'Independence Pass is narrow, steep and winding. Absolutely no vehicles over 35 feet in length, or vehicle/trailer combinations over 35 feet in length, are permitted between MP 47.2 (Aspen side) and MP 84.2 (Leadville/Twin Lakes side, about one mile west of the junction with US 24).' CDOT (May 19, 2026) gives the same mile points. Weller is ~8 mi east of Aspen, past MP 47.2, so it is INSIDE the restricted stretch; the old note's 'Aspen side, under the pass length limit' had it backwards. EKKO (23 ft) is unaffected. No criteria problem.
Length: the FS page states no site or spur length; inclusion_evidence's '~25 ft trailer cap' is from aggregators. Nothing official under 23 ft. No max_rig_ft written.
Water: the FS page says both 'potable water during the season' and 'Potable water is not available at this site.' Stored potable_water false left as is; a call to the district would settle it.
Season: the page's 'Dates and pricing listed under Developed Campgrounds' points to the forest camping page, which has no dates table now. No season recorded.
Pin 39.12086,-106.7204 = FS coordinates, at the campground entrance off CO-82. OK.
Waterfront 'not waterfront' kept: on NAIP the sites are on the slope north of CO-82; the Roaring Fork runs ~80-120 m south, beyond the highway and a continuous forest band.
